key_insight: An AI system can change even when its public name stays the same. The authors argue that meaningful version identifiers are needed to make these changes traceable for researchers and regulators.
problem_solved: Providers often update models and system integrations without changing public identifiers, making it difficult to reproduce findings or determine which system version was evaluated.
method: Identify the traceability gap caused by updates that leave public identifiers unchanged.
Argue for AI versioning that reflects meaningful changes to models and system integrations.
Frame versioning around the needs of scientific reproducibility and regulatory oversight.
impact: Meaningful versioning would help practitioners link evaluations and research results to specific AI system versions. It would also support more reliable comparisons and clearer regulatory oversight.
visual_elements: A fixed model-name label above a timeline of changing underlying systems.
A before-and-after diagram contrasting untracked updates with version-labeled updates.
A traceability chain connecting a version identifier to an evaluation result and regulatory record.
Researcher and regulator icons highlighting reproducibility and oversight.
paper_authors: Vasilios Mavroudis, Dan Ristea, Lauritz Morlock, Carlos Mougan
